# Close the Silence — Request for 1 Quarter of Talent-Systems Work

**To:** VP Talent · **From:** Product & Design · **Date:** 2026-08-18
**Ask:** Approve three changes to the application portal — surface real status, disclose the AI screen, and auto-close dead applications.

## The problem in one line
Candidates who pass our screen enter a queue with **no status, no timeline, and no guaranteed ending** — and the most common way our process concludes is that it doesn't.

## Where it breaks
Our own map has fifteen steps and four endings. One of those endings — *ghosted* — is the only step in the journey with **no outgoing path**: nothing leads out of it because nothing ever happens. It is not an edge case in the process; it is the process running to completion. *(`outcome-ghosted`: `failureMode`, `failureImpact: high`.)*

Two facts from the same map, worth reading together:

- The status of an application **does** change internally — a recruiter opens it, it moves in the queue — and none of those changes are ever shown to the candidate. *(`wait-in-silence`: `lineOfVisibility`, `orchestration: none`.)* We are not missing the information. We are declining to send it.
- An automated screen rejects candidates within 24 hours with **no human review, no disclosure that it was automated, and no correction path** — including when the miss came from our own resume parser. *(`ai-resume-screen`: `automation`, `failureMode`; `outcome-fast-rejection`: `painPoint`.)*

> A candidate spends ~43 minutes on the application and then waits ~6 weeks. About **one part in a thousand** of the experience is the part we designed. *(Computed from the map's own `duration` / `waitTime` fields — see caveat below.)*

## The fix
| What | Effort | Impact | Fixes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Surface the internal status we already hold — "in recruiter review, typically ~2 weeks" | Low | High | `wait-in-silence` *(must-fix)* |
| Disclose the automated screen, with one correction loop before rejection is final | Medium | High | `ai-resume-screen` *(must-fix)* |
| Auto-close sweep: when a role closes, every open application gets an answer | Low | High | `outcome-ghosted` *(must-fix)* |

None of these makes hiring faster. The hiring manager's shortlist takes as long as it takes — that constraint is real and we are not proposing to fight it. All three remove the *information vacuum* around an unavoidable wait.

## Cost of inaction
- **The worst outcome is currently the default one.** Ghosting is flagged in the map as the single most corrosive outcome for employer brand, and nothing in the current design prevents it. *(`outcome-ghosted`: `momentOfTruth`.)*
- **We lose qualified people invisibly.** A parsing miss and a genuine mismatch produce the identical automated rejection, and we never learn which one we just sent. *(`ai-resume-screen`: `failureMode`, `failureImpact: high`.)*
- **The bias runs in the direction of our stated goals.** Non-linear careers, career breaks, and non-standard formats score worst on the automated screen — the candidates our hiring goals specifically target are the ones the filter is least able to read. *(`ai-resume-screen`: `inclusionConsideration`, `risk`.)*
- **It compounds every cycle.** Each un-closed application is a person who tells other candidates what applying here is like.

## Why now
The three fixes sit on the three steps the map marks `priority: must-fix` in the post-submission half. Two of them are low effort, and one of those two — the auto-close sweep — eliminates an entire ending from the journey.

**Decision requested:** Approve one quarter of talent-systems work to ship status surfacing, AI-screen disclosure with a correction loop, and an auto-close sweep.

*Source: "Applying for a job through an online application portal" journey map (steps `ai-resume-screen`, `wait-in-silence`, `outcome-ghosted`). **This map carries no measured metrics** — it holds no drop-off rate, no time-to-response, no completion rate, and none are claimed here. The 43-minute and 6-week figures are derived from the map's own duration estimates, which were authored in conversation rather than instrumented. Recommend adding drop-off and time-to-response tracking alongside the first fix, so the second round of this brief can argue with numbers instead of structure.*
